stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M at $1.6B valuation
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding highlights the growing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness, as the DoD pushes for more robust capabilities. With the defense sector increasingly eyeing space, True Anomaly's traction indicates a bullish outlook for private security in orbit.
stories.soWhat: Investors clearly believe that space security is the next big thing, even if the rest of the world is still figuring out how to keep its satellites safe.

stories.head: NASA orders ISS crew to take shelter
stories.body: NASA instructed astronauts aboard the ISS to take refuge in a Crew Dragon due to concerns over Russian repairs. This decision underscores the growing unease regarding international cooperation in space, particularly with geopolitical tensions on the rise. The incident raises questions about operational safety and the reliability of international partners.
stories.soWhat: If NASA is this worried, it might be time for all of us to reconsider our assumptions about space safety.

stories.head: Billion-dollar space startups are multiplying
stories.body: A recent roundup revealed that the number of billion-dollar space startups is increasing, with companies like Astranis and Stoke Space leading the charge. Astranis recently raised $250 million for microGEO production, while Stoke secured $260 million for its fully-reusable medium-lift systems. This surge indicates a robust appetite for investment in space technology, as more players enter the market.
stories.soWhat: The unicorns are here, but the real question is whether they can deliver on their lofty valuations.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
